tests.name: the owner's grant is explicit, bounded to one principal, one authority and one project, and recorded
the owner's grant cannot be made for a principal without the scope, another owner's things, an inactive principal, or a project off its list
the owner's grant can be revoked, once and for good, and only by its owner
submitting records the statement, answers with a receipt, and the receipt is readable through the existing read path
submitting answers an identical retry with the same receipt and records nothing twice
submitting handles concurrent identical submissions: one record, one event, one receipt
submitting takes nothing about the owner, sponsor, requester, repository or project from the request
what is refused a principal without the scope, with the scope but no grant, or with only read access
what is refused an authority that was not granted, even a real one of the same owner; an authority of another owner reads the same
what is refused a revoked authority, even though the grant still stands
what is refused another project, another session, and another owner's session
what is refused a principal whose project list excludes the session's project
what is refused a commit the session did not produce
what is refused any claim but commit.attribution
what is refused a statement changed after it was signed: the claim, the commit, the payload, the time or the signature
what is refused a secret in the payload, a statement from the future, and one older than its commit
what is refused a suspended principal is refused before anything else
the database holds the line too refuses a machine submission without a live grant, for another claim, or by a principal that did not request the session
the database holds the line too refuses a grant whose principal lacks the scope, and the scope on a principal that approves
existing behaviour is unchanged the owner's route still takes any claim, records the owner as the actor, and has no principal
existing behaviour is unchanged existing scopes confer nothing: the read, request and push scopes cannot submit
the published contract is advertised in the API description, so a client can tell whether this server supports it
the published contract request, receipt and every error example conform to the description

note: Run against a disposable database with disposable signing keys and repositories. The hashes identify the files that were tested; re-run with `npm run contract:receipt` to reproduce.
